newsitem.title: UK: Large retailers gain market share in Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Large retailers gain market share in Latin America.

text.p: Supermarkets, department stores and discount retailers are thriving in Latin America at the expense of small traditional shops, according to a report published on Monday by Euromonitor, a market research company.
The report called "The Market for Retailing in Latin America" covers eight major Latin American markets and says large outlets are becoming increasingly popular with consumers.

"Latin America has a high proportion of food sales relative to the world's more developed markets. Euromonitor estimates that food accounts for over 80 percent of product spending for over half the region's population," the report said.
"Throughout the (Latin American) region modern distribution channels have been winning substantial ground from the traditional sector," it said.
Euromonitor said that a new class of consumers was emerging -- the low- to middle-income earners who are increasingly identified core drivers of growth.
This is most evident in Chile, where lower-middle income districts have become a boom area for shopping mall developments.

The situation is similar in Brazil, said Euromonitor, where lower-middle income households account for around 44 percent of the population and are increasingly being targeted by the country's major retailers.

Euromonitor predicts that "own-label" products will be one of the most important opportunities for growth over the next five years in Latin America and that convenience stores and large mixed retailers such as department stores will also grow.
